rationale:
Split into 5 children: 4 reuses of comparator-accepted declarations with byte-identical frozen types (orient_bound = dpf_pfc_imrep_orient_abs_apply_le, pairing_bound = dpf_pfc_imrep_pairing_integrable_abs_le, order_zero_current = cmcs_rc_order_zero_current, support_of_vanishing = rsd_cmr_support_subset_of_vanish) and 1 new lemma (integrand_bound = dimred_mbl_pfc_pullback_integrand_bound). The node is at depth 4 < 6.
Why split. Apart from a short assembly, the supplied proof consists of three independent, reusable obligations: (a) steps 1–3, the analytic estimate that the K-localized integrand θ·ξ(ω(f)∘Df) is Hⁿ⌞M-integrable with |I(ω)| ≤ Λ_Kⁿ·c_K·‖ω‖_∞; it rests on the a.e. unit-orientation bound and the pairing estimate, both already accepted in the DAG; (b) step 5, 'a linear functional on 𝒟ⁿ(U) with a zeroth-order bound is a current' (accepted as cmcs_rc_order_zero_current); (c) steps 7–8, 'a current that kills every form whose support misses a compact K ⊆ U has compact support inside K' (accepted as rsd_cmr_support_subset_of_vanish). The node's proof base 8ed075b contains only the frozen contract, so the accepted lemmas reach this node's Lean proof only as listed children, whose accepted candidates the runtime overlays. The new integrand_bound has exactly the hypotheses (K, O, f, R, Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0) of the sibling pf_boundary and of the identical-type node dor_lmb_pc_pushforward_current_exists, so it can be reused there.
Mapping of parent steps to children. Step 1 → orient_bound. Steps 2–3 → integrand_bound, which applies pairing_bound with C := K and F := 1_K·β_ω. Step 4 (linearity) stays in the parent. Step 5 → order_zero_current. Step 6 (vanishing away from f(K)) stays in the parent. Steps 7–8 → support_of_vanishing with K := f(K).
Parent assembly (checked in Lean):
1. integrand_bound gives A ≥ 0 such that, for every continuous ω and every B with ‖ω‖ ≤ B, the integrand is Hⁿ⌞M-integrable and |I(ω)| ≤ A·B. Each ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) is smooth, hence continuous (ContDiff.continuous). It has compact support, hence is bounded (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support).
2. Linearity. Pointwise, ((ω+η)(f x))∘Df(x) = ω(f x)∘Df(x) + η(f x)∘Df(x) and ((cω)(f x))∘Df(x) = c·(ω(f x)∘Df(x)), by ext and simp. Since ξ(x) is linear, integral_add (with integrability from 1) and integral_const_mul make I a LinearMap L : TestFormOn U n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ.
3. Applying order_zero_current with the constant c := A on every compact K' ⊆ U gives S : GeometricCurrentOn U n with S ω = L ω, which is the required integral.
4. Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0 gives x ∈ K for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x (ae_restrict_iff', ae_iff, measure_mono_null). Suppose Disjoint (tsupport ω) (f '' K). Then ω(f x) = 0 for x ∈ K (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), so the integrand vanishes a.e. and S ω = 0.
5. f '' K is compact, because f is continuous on K ⊆ O (IsCompact.image_of_continuousOn), and f '' K ⊆ U. Applying support_of_vanishing to S and f '' K gives S.support ⊆ f '' K and IsCompact S.support.

subproblems.title: IMRep orientations are a.e. unit: |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n). Then for Hⁿ⌞M-almost every x (i.e. μHE[n].restrict R.carrier-a.e.), every n-covector β ∈ Covector(ℝ^P, n) satisfies |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖, where ‖β‖ is the operator norm of β as a continuous alternating map.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict R.carrier), ∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) n, |R.orient x β| ≤ ‖β‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof ("Good points"); Simon 6.3.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 733–746). This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dpf_pfc_imrep_orient_abs_apply_le (candidate 056f1b9), reused with its byte-identical frozen type; the proof below is its accepted parent-supplied proof. In Simon 6.3.1, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, ξ(x) = τ₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ τ_n for an orthonormal basis τ₁, …, τ_n of the approximate tangent space. The contract encodes this as IsUnitOrientationOf: ⟨α, ξ⟩ = ±α(τ₁, …, τ_n). Notation: μ := μHE[n].restrict R.carrier and ξ := R.orient. For an n-covector β (a continuous alternating map (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ), ‖β‖ is its operator norm.
1. Reduction to a pointwise claim. By the field R.orients, for μ-a.e. x there is a subspace Q of ℝ^P with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n R.carrier x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q. The a.e. filter is upward closed (filter_upwards). So it suffices to prove: if IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q holds for some Q, then |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ for every n-covector β.
2. Unfolding the orientation. IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q provides an orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝ^P (its span is Q, which is not needed) such that either
   (a) ξ(x)(α) = α(τ) for all n-covectors α, or
   (b) ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all n-covectors α.
3. Operator-norm bound at τ. Let β be an n-covector.
   - The operator-norm inequality for continuous alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm) gives ‖β(τ)‖ ≤ ‖β‖ · ∏_{i<n} ‖τ_i‖.
   - Orthonormality gives ‖τ_i‖ = 1 for every i, so the product is 1. For n = 0 it is the empty product, also 1.
   - Since β(τ) is real, ‖β(τ)‖ = |β(τ)|. Hence |β(τ)| ≤ ‖β‖.
4. Both signs. In case (a), |ξ(x)(β)| = |β(τ)| ≤ ‖β‖. In case (b), |ξ(x)(β)| = |−β(τ)| = |β(τ)| ≤ ‖β‖ (abs_neg).
5. Conclusion. For μ-a.e. x, every n-covector β satisfies |R.orient x β| ≤ ‖β‖, which is the claim.
proof_key_steps: R.orients gives, μ-a.e., ξ(x) = ±(evaluation at an orthonormal τ).
Both signs give |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖; conclude by filter_upwards.

subproblems.title: Integrability and sup-norm estimate for the IMRep pairing with a bounded, compactly supported covector field
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, R = (M, θ, ξ) an IMRep U n, C ⊆ U compact and B ∈ ℝ. Let F : ℝ^P → Covector(ℝ^P, n) be a.e. strongly measurable for μ := Hⁿ⌞M (μHE[n].restrict R.carrier), with F(x) = 0 for all x ∉ C and ‖F(x)‖ ≤ B for all x. Then x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(F(x)) is μ-integrable, and |∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(F(x)) dHⁿ(x)| ≤ B · (∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dHⁿ).toReal.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U C : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (F : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n) (B : ℝ), IsCompact C → C ⊆ U → AEStronglyMeasurable F (μHE[n].restrict R.carrier) → (∀ x, x ∉ C → F x = 0) → (∀ x, ‖F x‖ ≤ B) → Integrable (fun x => (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x (F x)) (μHE[n].restrict R.carrier) ∧ |∫ x in R.carrier, (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x (F x) ∂μHE[n]| ≤ B * (∫⁻ x in R.carrier ∩ C, (R.mult x : ℝ≥0∞) ∂μHE[n]).toReal
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof (the K-localized integrand is integrable and |I(ω)| ≤ Λ_Kⁿ·c_K·‖ω‖_∞), i.e. the estimate behind Simon 6.2.24(2) (chapter-06.txt lines 414–425), which says that when M_W(T) < ∞ for W ⊂⊂ U, f_#T(ω) = ∫⟨ω(f(x)), df_x#ξ(x)⟩θ dHⁿ makes sense for C¹ f; the printed text leaves the integrability and the estimate to the reader, and they are supplied here. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dpf_pfc_imrep_pairing_integrable_abs_le (candidate 5c8c659), reused with its byte-identical frozen type; the proof below is its accepted parent-supplied proof. This proof uses the sibling theorem orient_bound (Submission.dpf_pfc_imrep_orient_abs_apply_le).
Notation:
- M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient, μ := μHE[n].restrict M;
- h(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(F(x)), with θ(x) viewed in ℝ;
- 1_C θ := C.indicator (fun y => (θ y : ℝ)) and g(x) := B·(1_C θ)(x).
1. C is measurable. C is compact, hence closed (IsCompact.isClosed), hence a Borel, i.e. measurable, set.
2. θ is measurable. θ : ℝ^P → ℕ is measurable (R.measurable_mult), and every function on ℕ is measurable (measurable_from_nat). So x ↦ (θ(x) : ℝ) is measurable, hence a.e. strongly measurable.
3. Restriction identity. Since C is measurable, μ.restrict C = (μHE[n].restrict M).restrict C = μHE[n].restrict (C ∩ M) = μHE[n].restrict (M ∩ C) (Measure.restrict_restrict, inter_comm).
4. 1_C θ and g are μ-integrable.
   - By R.locallyIntegrable_mult applied to the compact set C ⊆ U, ∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dμHE[n] ≠ ∞.
   - Since θ(x) ≥ 0, its extended norm ‖(θ(x) : ℝ)‖ₑ equals (θ(x) : ℝ≥0∞) (Real.enorm_natCast). By step 3, ∫⁻ ‖θ‖ₑ d(μ.restrict C) = ∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dμHE[n] < ∞.
   - With step 2, θ is integrable on C with respect to μ (IntegrableOn).
   - Hence 1_C θ is μ-integrable (integrable_indicator_iff, C measurable), and so is g = B·1_C θ (Integrable.const_mul).
5. h is μ-a.e. strongly measurable.
   - The evaluation map (ζ, β) ↦ ζ(β) from MultiVector P n × Covector (Euclid P) n to ℝ is continuous, since ζ ranges over continuous linear maps (continuous_fst.clm_apply continuous_snd).
   - ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient), and so is F (hypothesis). So x ↦ ξ(x)(F(x)) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂).
   - Multiplying by the measurable θ of step 2 preserves this (AEStronglyMeasurable.mul).
6. Domination |h| ≤ g μ-a.e. By orient_bound, for μ-a.e. x, |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ for all n-covectors β. Fix such an x.
   - If x ∈ C, then (1_C θ)(x) = θ(x). Using θ(x) ≥ 0 and ‖F(x)‖ ≤ B: |h(x)| = θ(x)·|ξ(x)(F(x))| ≤ θ(x)·‖F(x)‖ ≤ θ(x)·B = g(x).
   - If x ∉ C, then F(x) = 0 by hypothesis, so ξ(x)(F(x)) = 0 (ξ(x) is linear) and |h(x)| = 0. Also g(x) = B·0 = 0.
   Hence ‖h(x)‖ ≤ g(x) for μ-a.e. x.
7. Integrability. h is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (step 5) and dominated μ-a.e. by the μ-integrable g (steps 4 and 6). So h is μ-integrable (Integrable.mono'). This is the first conjunct.
8. Value of ∫ g dμ:
   ∫ g dμ = B·∫ 1_C θ dμ (integral_const_mul)
   = B·∫ θ d(μ.restrict C) (integral_indicator, C measurable)
   = B·∫ θ d(μHE[n].restrict (M ∩ C)) (step 3)
   = B·(∫⁻_{M∩C} ENNReal.ofReal(θ) dμHE[n]).toReal (integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae; θ ≥ 0 and is a.e. strongly measurable)
   = B·(∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dμHE[n]).toReal (ENNReal.ofReal_natCast).
9. Estimate. By definition of the set integral, ∫_M θ ξ(F) dμHE[n] = ∫ h dμ. Then |∫ h dμ| = ‖∫ h dμ‖ ≤ ∫ g dμ (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le, using integrability of g and step 6). By step 8 this gives |∫_M θ ξ(F) dμHE[n]| ≤ B·(∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dμHE[n]).toReal, the second conjunct.
proof_key_steps: C compact ⇒ measurable; θ measurable; μ.restrict C = Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ C).
Local integrability of θ on the compact C ⊆ U makes g = B·1_C θ μ-integrable.
h = θ·ξ(F) is a.e. strongly measurable via continuity of evaluation.
orient_bound together with F = 0 off C and ‖F‖ ≤ B gives |h| ≤ g μ-a.e.
Integrable.mono' gives integrability; |∫ h| ≤ ∫ g = B·(∫⁻_{M∩C} θ).toReal.

subproblems.title: Uniform integrability bound for the C¹ push-forward integrand localized to K (Simon 6.2.24(2))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U, K, O ⊆ ℝ^P, let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n; M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient) and let f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P. Assume that K is compact, K ⊆ U, Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0 (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), O is open, K ⊆ O and f is C¹ on O (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O). Then there is A ∈ ℝ with A ≥ 0 such that for every continuous n-form ω : ℝ^P → Covector(ℝ^P, n) (DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) and every B ∈ ℝ with ‖ω(z)‖ ≤ B for all z ∈ ℝ^P (operator norm of n-covectors): the function x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x)) is Hⁿ⌞M-integrable (with respect to μHE[n].restrict R.carrier), and |∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x)) dHⁿ(x)| ≤ A·B. Here Df(x) = fderiv ℝ f x and (α∘L)(v₁, …, vₙ) = α(Lv₁, …, Lvₙ) (α.compContinuousLinearMap L).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U K O : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (f : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (R.carrier \ K) = 0 → IsOpen O → K ⊆ O → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O → ∃ A : ℝ, 0 ≤ A ∧ ∀ (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (B : ℝ), Continuous ω → (∀ z, ‖ω z‖ ≤ B) → Integrable (fun x => (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x ((ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x))) (μHE[n].restrict R.carrier) ∧ |∫ x in R.carrier, (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x ((ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) ∂μHE[n]| ≤ A * B
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–3 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, Remark 2.24(2), chapter-06.txt lines 414–425: for C¹ f the push-forward f_#T(ω) = ∫⟨ω(f(x)), df_x#ξ(x)⟩θ dHⁿ makes sense), with the constant made explicit as A := Λⁿ·c_K and the sup-norm bound B of ω kept as a parameter. This proof uses the sibling theorem pairing_bound (Submission.dpf_pfc_imrep_pairing_integrable_abs_le).
Notation. M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient, Hⁿ := μHE[n], μ := Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M. Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x. ‖·‖ is the operator norm of linear maps and of n-covectors (continuous alternating maps). For an n-covector α and a linear map L, α∘L := α.compContinuousLinearMap L. c_K := (∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ).toReal, a nonnegative real number.
1. Derivative bound. Since f is C¹ on the open set O, the map x ↦ Df(x) is continuous on O (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen, with 1 ≤ 1). Since K ⊆ O is compact, there is Λ₀ ∈ ℝ with ‖Df(x)‖ ≤ Λ₀ for every x ∈ K (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn). Put Λ := max(Λ₀, 0). Then Λ ≥ 0 and ‖Df(x)‖ ≤ Λ for every x ∈ K.
2. The constant. Put A := Λⁿ·c_K. Since Λ ≥ 0 and c_K ≥ 0, A ≥ 0. A depends only on f, K and R. Now fix a continuous ω : ℝ^P → Covector(ℝ^P, n) and B ∈ ℝ with ‖ω(z)‖ ≤ B for all z; it remains to prove the two conjuncts for this ω and B. Note B ≥ ‖ω(0)‖ ≥ 0. K is compact, hence closed, hence a measurable set.
3. Continuity of the pulled-back covector on K. Let β(x) := ω(f(x))∘Df(x). The map x ↦ ω(f(x)) is continuous on K, since ω is continuous and f is continuous on O ⊇ K (ContDiffOn.continuousOn). The map x ↦ compContinuousLinearMapCLM(Df(x)) (the continuous linear map α ↦ α∘Df(x) on n-covectors) is continuous on K: it is the composition of x ↦ Df(x), continuous on K by step 1, with the continuous map L ↦ compContinuousLinearMapCLM L (ContinuousAlternatingMap.continuous_compContinuousLinearMapCLM). Applying a continuous family of continuous linear maps to a continuous family of vectors is continuous (ContinuousOn.clm_apply), and compContinuousLinearMapCLM(Df(x))(ω(f(x))) = β(x). Hence β is continuous on K.
4. The localized field. Let F := 1_K·β (Set.indicator), i.e. F(x) = β(x) for x ∈ K and F(x) = 0 for x ∉ K.
   (a) F is μ-a.e. strongly measurable: β is continuous on the measurable set K, so β is a.e. strongly measurable for μ restricted to K (ContinuousOn.aestronglyMeasurable); this is equivalent to a.e. strong measurability of the indicator F for μ (aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff, K measurable).
   (b) F(x) = 0 for every x ∉ K, by definition.
   (c) ‖F(x)‖ ≤ B·Λⁿ for every x. If x ∈ K, then by ContinuousAlternatingMap.norm_compContinuousLinearMap_le and Fintype.card (Fin n) = n, ‖F(x)‖ = ‖ω(f(x))∘Df(x)‖ ≤ ‖ω(f(x))‖·‖Df(x)‖ⁿ ≤ B·Λⁿ, using 0 ≤ ‖ω(f(x))‖ ≤ B, 0 ≤ ‖Df(x)‖ ≤ Λ (step 1), monotonicity of t ↦ tⁿ on [0, ∞), and B ≥ 0. If x ∉ K, then ‖F(x)‖ = 0 ≤ B·Λⁿ, because B ≥ 0 and Λ ≥ 0.
5. Pairing estimate. Apply pairing_bound with C := K (compact, K ⊆ U), the covector field F and the bound B·Λⁿ; its hypotheses are steps 4(a)–(c). It gives: x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(F(x)) is μ-integrable, and |∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(F(x)) dHⁿ(x)| ≤ B·Λⁿ·c_K.
6. μ-almost every point lies in K. Since M is measurable, "x ∈ K for μ-a.e. x" is equivalent (ae_restrict_iff') to "x ∈ M → x ∈ K for Hⁿ-a.e. x", i.e. to Hⁿ({x : x ∈ M and x ∉ K}) = 0. That set is M ∖ K, which is Hⁿ-null by hypothesis. For every x ∈ K we have F(x) = β(x), hence θ(x)·ξ(x)(F(x)) = θ(x)·ξ(x)(β(x)).
7. Conclusion. By step 6, the functions x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(F(x)) and x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(β(x)) agree μ-a.e. Integrability is invariant under a.e. equality (Integrable.congr), so by step 5 the function x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x)) is μ-integrable; this is the first conjunct. The two integrals agree (integral_congr_ae), so |∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x)) dHⁿ(x)| = |∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(F(x)) dHⁿ(x)| ≤ B·Λⁿ·c_K = A·B; this is the second conjunct. ∎
proof_key_steps: Df is continuous on the open O ⊇ K, so Λ := max(sup_K ‖Df‖, 0) is finite; put A := Λⁿ·c_K ≥ 0 with c_K := (∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ).toReal.
For continuous ω with ‖ω‖ ≤ B, β(x) = ω(f(x))∘Df(x) is continuous on K, so F := 1_K·β is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, vanishes off K and satisfies ‖F‖ ≤ B·Λⁿ (norm_compContinuousLinearMap_le).
pairing_bound with C := K gives integrability of θ·ξ(F) and |∫_M θ·ξ(F) dHⁿ| ≤ B·Λⁿ·c_K.
Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0 makes θ·ξ(F) = θ·ξ(β) μ-a.e., which transfers integrability and gives the bound A·B.

subproblems.title: A linear functional on 𝒟ⁿ(U) with zeroth-order bounds on every compact subset of U is a current
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, and let L : 𝒟ⁿ(U) → ℝ be ℝ-linear (L : TestFormOn U n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ). Suppose that for every compact K ⊆ U there is c ∈ ℝ such that |L(ω)| ≤ c·M for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ K and every M ∈ ℝ with ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ M for all x ∈ ℝ^P (‖·‖ the operator norm on n-covectors). Then there is a current S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n, i.e. L together with Simon's sequential continuity) with S(ω) = L(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (L : TestFormOn U n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ (ω : TestFormOn U n) (M : ℝ), tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ K → (∀ x, ‖(ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x‖ ≤ M) → |L ω| ≤ c * M) → ∃ S : GeometricCurrentOn U n, ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, S ω = L ω
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof (continuity of I in Simon's sequential test-form topology), stated for an arbitrary linear functional L satisfying the zeroth-order estimate that step 5 uses; Simon 6.2.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 192–194: an n-current in U is a continuous linear functional on 𝒟ⁿ(U)). This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.cmcs_rc_order_zero_current (candidate 4935893), reused with its byte-identical frozen type; the proof below is its accepted parent-supplied proof.

For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) write ω̂ := (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) for its underlying form, and ‖·‖ for the operator norm of n-covectors.

1. (Reduction.) A GeometricCurrentOn U n is a structure ⟨T₀, h⟩ consisting of a linear map T₀ : TestFormOn U n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ and a proof h that T₀(ω_j) → 0 for every sequence (ω_j) with TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0; its value S(ω) is T₀(ω). Take T₀ := L. Then S(ω) = L(ω) holds by definition for every ω, and it remains to prove: if (ω_j)_{j∈ℕ} in 𝒟ⁿ(U) satisfies TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0, then L(ω_j) → 0 in ℝ.

2. (Unpacking the convergence.) By definition of TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0 there is a compact K ⊆ U with tsupport ω̂_j ⊆ K for all j such that, for every k ∈ ℕ, iteratedFDeriv ℝ k ω̂_j → iteratedFDeriv ℝ k 0̂ uniformly on K, where 0̂ is the underlying form of the zero test form, i.e. the zero function. Apply the hypothesis to this compact K ⊆ U to obtain c ∈ ℝ with |L(ω)| ≤ c·M whenever ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), tsupport ω̂ ⊆ K and ‖ω̂(x)‖ ≤ M for all x.

3. (Zeroth-order smallness on K.) For every function G and point x, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 G x‖ = ‖G(x)‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero). In particular ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0̂ x‖ = ‖0̂(x)‖ = 0, so iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0̂ x = 0 for every x. Uniform convergence for k = 0, in metric form (Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff together with eventually_atTop), says: for every η > 0 there is N such that dist(iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0̂ x, iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω̂_j x) < η for all j ≥ N and all x ∈ K. This distance equals dist(0, iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω̂_j x) = ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω̂_j x‖ = ‖ω̂_j(x)‖ (dist_zero_left). Hence ‖ω̂_j(x)‖ < η for all j ≥ N and all x ∈ K.

4. (Off K.) If x ∉ K, then x ∉ tsupport ω̂_j (because tsupport ω̂_j ⊆ K), so ω̂_j(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and ‖ω̂_j(x)‖ = 0 ≤ η. With step 3: for every j ≥ N, ‖ω̂_j(x)‖ ≤ η for all x ∈ ℝ^P.

5. (Conclusion.) Let δ > 0 and put η := δ/(|c| + 1) > 0; let N be as in step 3 for this η. For j ≥ N, the hypothesis applied to ω := ω_j and M := η (valid by tsupport ω̂_j ⊆ K and step 4) gives
   |L(ω_j) − 0| = |L(ω_j)| ≤ c·η ≤ |c|·η = δ·|c|/(|c| + 1) < δ,
   using c ≤ |c|, η ≥ 0, δ > 0 and |c| < |c| + 1. Since δ > 0 was arbitrary, L(ω_j) → 0 (Metric.tendsto_atTop). This is the continuity requirement, so S := ⟨L, h⟩ is a GeometricCurrentOn U n with S(ω) = L(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). ∎
proof_key_steps: Take S := ⟨L, h⟩; then S(ω) = L(ω) by definition, so only L(ω_j) → 0 for TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0 must be shown.
TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0 gives a compact K ⊆ U containing every tsupport ω_j and uniform convergence on K of the order-0 derivatives; take the constant c for this K.
‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 G x‖ = ‖G(x)‖ and the limit form is 0, so for every η > 0 eventually ‖ω_j(x)‖ < η on K; off K, ω_j(x) = 0.
With η = δ/(|c|+1): eventually |L(ω_j)| ≤ c·η ≤ |c|·η < δ, hence L(ω_j) → 0.

subproblems.title: A current vanishing on forms supported away from a compact set has compact support inside it
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, K ⊆ U compact, and F ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with F(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) whose topological support is disjoint from K. Then spt F ⊆ K and spt F is compact. Here spt F = U ∖ Z(F) (GeometricCurrentOn.support), Z(F) being the union of all open W with closure(W) compact, closure(W) ⊆ U and F(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U K : Set (Euclid P)) (F : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) K → F ω = 0) → F.support ⊆ K ∧ IsCompact F.support
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 7–8 of the parent proof (spt Q ⊆ f(K) and compactness of spt Q), isolated for an arbitrary current F ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and an arbitrary compact K ⊆ U; the parent applies it to F := Q and the compact set f(K) ⊆ U. Simon 6.2.11 (chapter-06.txt lines 296–301) defines spt T as U minus the union of the open sets on which T vanishes. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.rsd_cmr_support_subset_of_vanish (candidate 02c6122), reused with its byte-identical frozen type; the proof below is its accepted parent-supplied proof.

1. Points of U ∖ K are not in spt F. Let y ∈ U ∖ K. Since U is open and K is closed (compact), U ∖ K is open (IsOpen.sdiff), so there is s > 0 with B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K. Put W := B_{s/2}(y).
 (a) W is open and y ∈ W.
 (b) closure(W) ⊆ B̄_{s/2}(y) ⊆ B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K ⊆ U.
 (c) closure(W) is compact, as a closed subset of the compact closed ball B̄_{s/2}(y) (ℝ^P is proper).
 (d) If ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) and tsupport ω ⊆ W, then tsupport ω ⊆ B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K is disjoint from K, so F(ω) = 0.
 By (a)-(d), W is one of the sets whose union is Z(F), so y ∈ Z(F) and y ∉ spt F.

2. spt F ⊆ K. By definition spt F ⊆ U, and by step 1 no point of U ∖ K lies in spt F.

3. Compactness. From spt F = U ∖ Z(F), spt F ⊆ K and K ⊆ U, we get spt F = K ∖ Z(F). Z(F) is open, as a union of open sets (isOpen_zeroRegion). So K ∖ Z(F) is a closed subset of the compact set K, hence compact (IsCompact.diff). ∎
proof_key_steps: For y ∈ U ∖ K, a ball B_{s/2}(y) with closure in U ∖ K is a relatively compact zero set of F, so y ∉ spt F.
Hence spt F ⊆ K, and spt F = K ∖ Z(F) is compact because Z(F) is open.
